events.summary: In the 1960s, biologists introduced wolves to Coronation Island in Alaska after deer overran it and decimated the forest understory. The wolves ate all the deer and, with nothing left to eat, starved. About 50 years later, the wolves of Pleasant Island Alaska found themselves in a similar situation: living on an island in the Pacific with no deer left to eat. The wolves of Pleasant Island, however, have not died out. Instead, theyve broadened their palate to include sea otters. What scientists dont know is how widespread this surf-and-turf phenomenon is. events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.

Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. CPP showcases art by anyone with experiences relating to chronic pain. Some of our artists have created for decades, and others have only just begun. events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.

Evergreen Blvd. Vancouver, WA 98660. Parking is available in the east lot next to the Academy. To purchase tickets, please visit our events page at: https://www.thehistorictrust.org/calendar/providence-academy-concert/. Questions? Call us at 360-992-1800. The Historic Trust would like to thank their sponsor, Columbia Invest & Insure, a program of Columbia Credit Union.

events.summary: Folkloric writing can take many forms. From the overtly fantastical to the strangely realistic, the old tales are flexible. They shift over times and tellers. Their presence in our work can move from obvious to subtle. In this course, we’ll study writing that engages with folklore in a wide variety of ways: speculative memoir that tangles with witch tales, poems that draw on botanical lore, short story fairy tale retellings, mythic poetry and fiction, and more. Through discussion, reflection, and generative writing exercises, we’ll consider how we use old stories and lore in our own work. Suitable for writers at all stages, you can use this course to start a new project or continue work on an ongoing one. Prose writers, poets, and all writers between are welcome. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts. Apply here for the liaison position.

events.summary: Throughout this six week course, students will look at the many ways in which humans are connected to our natural surroundings, both urban and remote. Weather, soil, plants, wildlife, changing systems, and more will all be explored. By delving into the inherent close relationship humans have with our natural world, each student’s path to writing their own stories using the natural world as scaffolding will emerge. Each lesson will be designed to unlock the storyteller within by encouraging observation, reading, and learning about natural systems. Participants will read various forms of nature prose and poetry including work by Mary Oliver, Robin Wall Kimmerer, Barbara Kingsolver, Merlin Sheldrake, Richard Powers, Robert Macfarlane, and more. These readings and the resulting discussions will then serve as a springboard to developing personal tone and style. Through guided in-class exercises students will work to develop their own narrative voice. Each step in the course will hone in on students’ unique narrative perspectives that reflects their own personal connections to the natural world. The in-class writing prompts will often draw on lived experiences and are intended to help students find their voice. Whether it’s remembering a favorite hike, gardening in their own backyard, watching a bird from their apartment window, cloud watching, traveling further afield into the wilderness, swimming, or walking a creek path, students will have opportunities to use memory to capture the feeling of decompressing in nature in words. Students will explore various forms and literary devices and styles in the process. Students will then have the opportunity to share these free-writes in class to get feedback from peers and the instructor. By reading the greats and engaging with the natural world from a personal standpoint, students will develop their understanding of ecology and our human connection to it as a species. By the end of the course, acknowledging human interconnectivity with nature may very well become an inherent part of students’ writing process. This course invites students to dig deep, observe the world around them, slow down, bask in the beauty of the PNW, and discover how their own unique stories can spring from nature. Access Program We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. events.summary: My Three Fathers \(Sibylline Press\) is a memoir of reckoning, forgiveness, and the fragile work of choosing what to carry forward. Between her absent Cuban immigrant birth father, her adopted Cherokee-Jewish Army soldier father, and her Iranian stepfather, Jamie Leigh Lorente grows up at the crossroads of war, migration, and cultural fracture. Each father offers a different version of love and absence, leaving marks she will spend years trying to understand. Their lives and their stories reveal the generational wounds she inherits and the complicated ways family is both formed and fractured. She thinks about what caused her to marry so young and to the wrong man. As a mother of three sons, she is determined to give them what she never had: stability, presence, a sense of being rooted. Yet as she dismantles the mythologies she has long carried about her fathers, and about herself, she recognizes the patterns she has repeated. Lorente will be joined in conversation by Sonya Lea, author of Wondering Who You Are. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/lorente-9798897400287

events.summary: Reduce your social anxiety. Increase your confidence. Learn to navigate the world. Begin changing your psychology. Our newest class series isn't therapy, but it is incredibly therapeutic. We'll leverage the power of applied \(or process\) improvisation to bring the tools of improv to our daily lives. We'll anchor much of our work in the teachings & approaches of Augusto Boal and Paulo Friere, two educators who helped bring this style of improvisation to the world. Together, we'll learn how to: 🗣️ Share our most powerful life stories with honesty & vulnerability 💥 Explore those stories with creativity & support 👁️ See & experience our lives through the lens of others 💪🏼 Discover our psychological strengths and, most importantly... ❤️ Evolve our relationships through the power of insight 🗣️ 1:1 Sessions Included The practice of applied improvisation is fun, but also requires vulnerability. For this reason, this series includes a 30-60min 1:1 session with your teacher. In these virtual sessions, we'll discuss and celebrate your breakthroughs and then examine the patterns that have emerged from your work that might be holding you back from even deeper successes.

events.summary: Marsha Blovotnik is angry. So angry! The whole world is *fakakte*, but for this Leftie Jewish Lesbian, it’s her sister Janice who really burns her *tuchus*. Janice invites herself over for *Shabbos* dinner and then shows up three minutes early. Who does that?!? Just before her sister arrives, a mysterious ancestor gives Marsha a pot of magical chicken soup with the power to cure the world of its woes — if only Marsha can cool down enough to share a bowl of soup with her sister. A buoyant, crackling comedy about how to live in a dumpster fire.

events.summary: Rock, Revolution. *LIZZIE* Brings America's Favorite Murder Mystery to Portland Marin Summer Theater and Bridgetown Conservatory of Musical Theatre present *LIZZIE* Music by Steven Cheslik-deMeyer, Alan Stevens Hewitt & Tim Maner Book and Lyrics by Tim Maner & Steven Cheslik-deMeyer What really happened inside the Borden house? Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. The show has earned international acclaim, with productions in more than 100 theaters across 11 countries and multiple Best Musical awards. More information and tickets can be found at https:\\\\lizziepdx.com.
events.title: LIZZIE

events.summary: Step into a slippery world where the line between truth and fiction is all in the packaging. It’s 1936, and a pair of passionate filmmakers have landed their next big project: a sweeping Spanish Civil War film with the potential to change American hearts and minds. It just happens to be bankrolled by the KGB. Spain by Jen Silverman is a seductive and tense thriller about the power of art to change the world – for better and for worse. One of the most ambitious productions in recent Profile history, Spain is a grand cross-disciplinary spectacle featuring multiple partnerships with arts organizations throughout Portland, including live opera developed in partnership with Portland Opera, and both recorded and live music performed by musicians with 45th Parallel!

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.
events.title: Anthropology

events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. Show Dates: October 15 – November 1, 2026 Thu – Sat at 7:30pm, Sun at 2pm Special Dates: Thursday, October 15 is a preview performance, with discounted tickets. Friday, October 16, is Opening Night! Sat, Oct. 24th – ASL Interpreted Performance Sun, Oct. 25th – Audio Described Performance
events.title: The Woman In Black

events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: MUSUBI is an international DJ, producer, and artist quickly rising as one of the most exciting new names in the music circuit. Born and raised in San Francisco, now based between Los Angeles and New York City, she’s building a reputation for sets that are as unpredictable as they are unforgettable. With a deep-rooted passion for music and connection, MUSUBI brings unmatched energy and range to every stage. Her sound is fluid and evolving, shaped by her instincts and the spaces she plays — from underground club nights to major festival stages. Refusing to be one dimensional, her base is house music with a twist. Recognized for her ability to control and elevate a crowd, she’s already played alongside some of the industry’s biggest names including Kaytranada, Eric Prydz, Joji, A-Trak, Snoop Dogg, Snakehips, SG Lewis, and Doechii just to name a few. Her resume includes main stage performances at festivals like Escape Halloween, Fvded In The Park, Countdown NYE, and Breakaway Music Festival — with more on the horizon. In addition to her growing list of high-profile appearances, MUSUBI has cultivated a loyal and rapidly expanding fanbase. Known for consistently packing out venues across multiple cities and countries, she continues to sell out shows nationwide — a testament to her resonance with audiences and the unique experience she brings to every performance. Now stepping into her role as a producer, MUSUBI is translating her live energy into original releases, continuing to define her sound while expanding her reach. Whether behind the decks or in the studio, she’s carving out a lane entirely her own. You can find her mixes and music on all major streaming platforms , and catch her live in cities across the map.
events.title: MUSUBI

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.
events.title: Georgina Reskala ·

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

Drop-in participation welcome! Wild Goose \(“Dayan” 大雁 in Chinese\) Qigong is an ancient Chinese Taoist movement art that nurtures one’s inner energy – Qi – and restores a healthy mind and body. The 64 movement first set mimics the wild goose, a highly revered animal of ancient China. With regular practice one can learn to access Qi for self-healing, restore vital energy, and strengthen one’s immune system to promote a healthy, balanced, and long life. Join Wen Wu School Portland for weekly Wild Goose Qigong practice classes, which include tai chi warm-ups, acupressure self-massage, and walking meditation through the Garden. events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: This is a weekend-long event to celebrate Samhain and the thinning of the veil! You don't need an RSVP to attend, but you'll get a free surprise when you do! All workshops, and readers are on a first come basis at varying costs. events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: The Literary Arts Bookstore and Cafe are thrilled to welcome Lit Mic for another immersive writing workshop! Participants will search for clues, interview witnesses, and conduct their own investigation via creative writing prompts and sharing to solve the murder. Detective Jack Argentine is back, and this time, it’s magical. It’s nearly Halloween, and a coven of honest-to-goodness witches is hosting their Biannual Bewitchment Ball. But something has gone terribly wrong, and one of the coven members is dead! Through independent and guided writing prompts, investigation, and conversations with live witchy actors, it’s up to YOU to help Detective Argentine figure out if this is just a spell gone wrong… or a case of Halloween Homicide. But the witching hour is close at hand; if the clock strikes midnight, the witches will be gone back to their home, and this case will vanish like mist in the night. Are you up for the task? About Lit Mic: Portland Lit Mic is a community-oriented organization, dedicated to getting writers from all backgrounds together. Founded as a writers-only open mic by Portland State Alumni Jordan Marzka and Grace Lawrence, the two have gone on to plan and host immersive writing workshops and reading series. You can catch their open mic every second Friday of the month at Rose City Book Pub, or keep up on their current events by following their Instagram @portlandlitmic Content warning—while Murder in the Bookstore is intended to be fun for all, themes of murder/violence and mild gore will be present. Tickets are $15 and include a souvenir notebook to take down clues.

events.summary: The 43rd season of the Beaverton Symphony Orchestra begins with a monument of the Romantic period and arguably one of the most emotionally powerful works of orchestral writing ever penned to paper. Tchaikovsky’s Pathétique—his sixth and final symphony—is suffused with passion and teeming with lively virtuosity and sweeping lyricism. Those who enjoy the Romanticism of Tchaikovsky’s other symphonies, ballets, and overtures will be moved… maybe to tears. While Tchaikovsky is known for wearing his heart on his sleeve, in the Pathétique he throws his heart into the crowd, laying bare every emotion in its unforgettable final moments. The concert will also include Bedrich Smetana’s iconic depiction of the largest river in the Czech Republic, The Moldau. Painting with sound, Smetana carries us down the river passing through forests, meadows, a country wedding, dancing mermaids, and ancient ruins overlooking its banks. Two brief tone poems by Anatoly Lyadov will kick off this season-opening concert inspired by two legendary figures from Slavic folklore: the fearsome witch Baba Yaga and the mysterious spirit Kikimora. Join the Beaverton Symphony Orchestra as we open our 43rd season on October 30 and November 1, 2026, at Village Church in Beaverton.

events.summary: Although he was born in the industrial heart of New Jersey, Red’s mother Maggie made damn sure that he would be reared on folk and country music. She served up a steady diet of Country tunes from Karen Dalton to Patsy Cline to Dwight Yoakam on the kitchen radio day after day. Red’s father, a lifelong bass player, took it from there, teaching him banjo, bass, and guitar. Forever restless, Red ventured through dozens of genres before returning to his Country roots. A firm believer that an artist’s greatest work is their life, Red always sought adventure beyond music in his wildly vacillating careers. Over only the past 5, he spent time working in National Parks and schools, bars and the backcountry, and most recently spending several years between the emergency department and ambulances across the country. Now settled into his high desert home Flagstaff, Arizona, Red has hit the road playing country music full tilt. In this first barnstorming year, he and his band will have played 31 states over 10 separate tours, logging over 25,000 miles and playing well over 250 shows a year with no end in sight. A first responder, passionate outdoorsman, recovering alcoholic, and heartbroken songwriter, whatever authenticity the country audience craves has been earned through his life, not place of birth. A self-proclaimed “Western fraud,” Red makes no effort to fit the country mold and rather draws from the reality of his life. Stranger-than-fiction characters and experiences from a life on the road mingle with honest, vulnerable expressions of a tumultuous life. events.summary: The year is 2056. We always knew they were out there…we just didn’t know they would attack so soon. Our city has fallen. Alien invaders and their cyborg forces have reduced the streets to rubble, and the few remaining survivors are doing whatever they can to escape. As if that weren’t enough, the destruction has brought another threat out of the shadows: zombies. This year’s interactive, no-contact haunted theatre drops you into the middle of the invasion. Choose how you face the apocalypse: Join the Resistance Rent an optional laser-tag weapon \(\+$2\) and fight back. The equipment uses a safe, invisible infrared beam to activate designated targets and trigger special effects as you move through the theatre. Become a Refugee Prefer not to use laser tag? Make your way through the ruined city as a refugee, trying to escape with your life while danger waits around every corner. Apocalypse in the Grove may include fog, laser lighting, loud noises, strobe effects, simulated fire, cold sparks, sudden scares, and intense theatrical environments. Will you join the resistance—or simply try to survive? When you purchase a ticket, you purchase a reservation for a 30 minute window. You must arrive in this timeframe or your entry could be delayed or denied. There are 6 people in each tour of the haunted theatre. This experience is wheelchair accessible. Children 12 and under MUST be accompanied by an adult.

events.summary: Step into a sinful, spooky night of 1920s hot jazz and burlesque with the Ne Plus Ultra Jass Orchestra at historic Old Liberty Theater. Get ready for a sinful, spooky night of hot jazz, burlesque, and vintage glamour! The Ne Plus Ultra Jass Orchestra brings its 12-piece ensemble to the historic Old Liberty Theater in downtown Ridgefield for one night only with Hot Rhythms: A Sinful Cabaret Burlesque Revue. Known for presenting the hottest and most authentic classic jazz of the 1920s and 1930s, the Ne Plus Ultra Jass Orchestra will take you back to the era of Prohibition with a wicked collection of ghoulish, sultry, and downright irresistible tunes. Joining the orchestra for this special Halloween-weekend performance are acclaimed Pacific Northwest burlesque performers Natasha Riot, Cruz Daniels, and Wolfgang X. Together, the performers and musicians bring the storytelling, theatricality, and playful sensuality of classic burlesque to life, with the dancers performing alongside the live orchestra. Expect vintage jazz. Sinful rhythms. Spooky surprises. And a night of cabaret decadence you won't soon forget. This is a one-night-only event, so come dressed for the occasion, grab a drink, and prepare to be transported to a darker, sexier side of the Jazz Age. General Admission : $30 VIP Table: $150 A very limited number of premium VIP tables are available. Each VIP table includes admission for up to four guests plus one bottle of champagne. VIP tables are extremely limited and are expected to sell quickly. This event is strictly 21 and over. A Note About the Performance Burlesque is a theatrical art form rooted in comedy, dance, music, costume, and storytelling. The style of burlesque presented in this performance draws particularly from the classic burlesque tradition that developed in the early 20th century. Performances may include the tasteful removal of clothing as part of the storytelling and theatrical presentation. Performers do not become fully nude. This is a theatrical burlesque performance, not strip club or gentlemen's club style dancing. Some performers may interact with members of the audience as part of their acts. Consent is always key, and performers will not interact with audience members who appear uncomfortable. Tipping performers is an important part of burlesque culture. If you'd like to show your appreciation, please bring plenty of $1 bills. Cash will be available for withdrawal at the event, and QR codes will also be available for digital tips to individual performers. The content is adult in nature, but the overall performance would be comparable to approximately a PG-13 rating in film. Parking Street parking is available throughout downtown Ridgefield, but spaces can be limited, particularly for popular events. We recommend arriving early to allow time to find parking and get settled before the performance. Event Schedule 6:45 PM - Doors Open 7:30 PM - Performance Begins This event is made possible through the generosity of our media sponsor, the Clark County Historical Museum TICKETS ARE NON-REFUNDABLE/NON-TRASFERABLE
events.title: Hot Rhythms: A Sinful Cabaret Burlesque Revue

events.summary: Rock, Revolution. *LIZZIE* Brings America's Favorite Murder Mystery to Portland Marin Summer Theater and Bridgetown Conservatory of Musical Theatre present *LIZZIE* Music by Steven Cheslik-deMeyer, Alan Stevens Hewitt & Tim Maner Book and Lyrics by Tim Maner & Steven Cheslik-deMeyer What really happened inside the Borden house? Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. The show has earned international acclaim, with productions in more than 100 theaters across 11 countries and multiple Best Musical awards. More information and tickets can be found at https:\\\\lizziepdx.com.

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. Show Dates: October 15 – November 1, 2026 Thu – Sat at 7:30pm, Sun at 2pm Special Dates: Thursday, October 15 is a preview performance, with discounted tickets. Friday, October 16, is Opening Night! Sat, Oct. 24th – ASL Interpreted Performance Sun, Oct. 25th – Audio Described Performance
events.title: The Woman In Black

events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: 7pm doors 8pm show All ages welcome Great Lake Swimmers Featuring a blend of acoustic instruments, rural soundscapes, and wistful vocals, Great Lake Swimmers are a critically acclaimed indie-folk group led by Tony Dekker. Based in Southern Ontario, the group emerged in the early 2000s with a succession of heavily atmospheric albums recorded in old silos and rural country churches. The music developed in that pastoral warmth, performed and recorded in acoustically resonant and historical locales with a revolving cast of personnel. They are renowned for homespun folk and lush, intimate Americana in their live shows. Their newest album, Caught Light, released in October 2025, is their most immediate and instinctive album to date. Recorded in just five days in Ontario's Ganaraska Forest with producer Darcy Yates \(Bahamas\) and engineer Jimmy Bowskill \(Blue Rodeo\), it draws warmth from early '70s folk-pop while embracing a new spontaneity and directness in Dekker's songwriting. Great Lake Swimmers have been shortlisted for the prestigious Polaris Music Prize and nominated twice for Canada's Juno Awards, with the CBC calling them "a national treasure." "A stunning variety of tones and textures... nothing less than both cerebral and sublime" - American Songwriter, 4/5 "It floats from country to folk to indie rock and back again... a sharp-toothed but achingly beautiful portrait of the natural world and the human condition." - New Noise Magazine "Dekker's preoccupation with the Canadian state of mind flourishes in his lyrics. Few songwriters are able to convey the country's harsh beauty as well. ...Canadian folk tradition personified in the 21st century" - Exclaim! Website: https://greatlakeswimmers.com

events.summary: Since her debut, Soraya has solidified herself as a key tastemaker and driving force in California’s rising indie dance scene. Known for her dynamic and high-energy performances, the Filipino-American producer and DJ crafts genre-defying sets that pulse between house, techno, and indie dance. Her ability to fuse underground club aesthetics with euphoric, late-night energy has earned her a reputation as a must-see selector– captivating crowds across the United States. Her debut release ‘Brain Delay’ was released in early 2025 on Adam Ten & Mita Gami’s Maccabi House imprint alongside Broken Hill. The track garnered support from artists across the globe including Adam Ten, Mita Gami, Sam Shure, Audio Junkies, Enamour, Rafael, and more- alongside reaching Top 10 on Beatport’s Indie Dance Charts in the first day and has remained there since its release. In the past few years, Soraya has been a fixture at both major venues and underground parties, earning residencies and bookings at standout events such as Definition LA, Day Trip, Area15 Las Vegas, Midnight Lovers LA, Monarch SF, Music is 4 Lovers, Academy LA, and FNGRS CRSSD. She has shared stages with some of iconic names in the industry– providing direct support for artists like Mita Gami, Chaim, Deer Jade, Super Flu, andhim, Eli & Fur, Session Victim, and more. With a meticulous approach to sound design and a deep-rooted love for the underground, Soraya’s new chapter promises to further cement her as a force in the scene—one who doesn’t just play the music but shapes its future.
events.title: Soraya

events.summary: Always on the go as one of the Pacific Northwest’s most trusted guitarists, Chance Hayden has performed avidly since the mid-00s as a chameleon-like musician who fluidly adapts through jazz, blues, funk and soul. Hayden's albums Get Somethin’ \(2018\) and Grab & Go \(2020\) were followed by the stand-alone single Shag Bag \(2022\) featuring iconic keyboardist Ronnie Foster of 70s-era George Benson fame. Most recently, Hayden centered his creative focus around the seldom heard baritone guitar with Baritone Gold \(2024\), showcasing a dozen 60s-inspired originals that span from surf to soul-blues with classic soundtrack vibes. Hayden’s works have been featured in television and film, including the Sony Pictures \#1 box office hit The Perfect Guy, the award-winning BET series Being Mary Jane and the popular Netflix series The Waterfront.

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.
events.title: Georgina Reskala ·

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

events.summary: Treats for Fur Babies, Treats for Humans—Only Until They Last… On Oct. 31, Sidereus Winery celebrates Joey’s birthday, our beloved winery dog, which is also on the spooky day of Halloween. Come by for a glass and pick up a special treat for your fur baby that you can take home or have your dog enjoy on-site. Please note that dogs are welcome on our deck and lawn areas—\[only Joey can come in the Sidereus Tasting House\]. For adults, join in the spirit of Halloween in costume with your friends. We’ll have treats for you too, while supplies last. Joey’s Story: A 4-pound Puff, the Smartest Dog, Best Friends Sidereus winery owners Skip and Ruth Tarr picked up Joey on Dec. 26, 2019 from a breeder in Scappoose, when he weighed only 4 pound. Since then, we think that Joey is the BEST and smartest dog in the whole world. Why? Ruth says that Joey is the smartest dog because after he learned more than 60 words, she quit counting. She elaborates that when she and Skip went through training with Joey, the trainer said that he was really training her and Skip, which explains how Joey started out knowing only his name and ‘sit,’ but his knowledge and vocabulary increased significantly after Ruth and Skip’s training was complete. Melissa, Sidereus wine tasting associate, also perfected Joey’s dance moves by teaching him how to ‘twirl.’ Joeys favorite things are steak, cauliflower, and playing with the ball and the water hose. His most favorite person is our winemaker Jason, who has Joey as a helper in winery production. Joey became an instant celebrity, made famous earlier this year when he was on-camera with Andy Carson of Good Day Oregon in a special feature that Andy led at Sidereus Winery last July. Joey is a small dog in stature. With all the coyotes in our vineyard are, he isn’t able to be outside by himself, as he thinks he’s a giant—but it’s really his heart that is big. He hasn’t found a human yet whom hasn’t become a friend.
events.title: Wicked Treats for Dogs & Humans, Joey's Birthday at Sidereus Winery

events.summary: The Moreland Theater is proud to present WALLACE AND GROMIT: THE CURSE OF THE WERE-RABBIT (2005) as part of the Halloween themed Spooky Family Matinees screening series! The screening on Halloween 10/31 will feature a kids/family costume contest pre-show with prizes for our top three winners! So, come early if you'd like to participate. It's 'vege-mania' in Wallace and Gromit's neighborhood, and our two enterprising chums are cashing in with their humane pest-control outfit, "Anti-Pesto." With only days to go before the annual Giant Vegetable Competition, business is booming, but Wallace & Gromit are finding out that running a "humane" pest control outfit has its drawbacks as their West Wallaby Street home fills to the brim with captive rabbits. Suddenly, a huge, mysterious, veg-ravaging "beast" begins attacking the town's sacred vegetable plots at night, and the competition hostess, Lady Tottington, commissions Anti-Pesto to catch it and save the day. Lying in wait, however, is Lady Tottington's snobby suitor, Victor Quartermaine, who'd rather shoot the beast and secure the position of local hero-not to mention Lady Tottingon's hand in marriage. With the fate of the competition in the balance, Lady Tottington is eventually forced to allow Victor to hunt down the vegetable chomping marauder. Little does she know that Victor's real intent could have dire consequences for her ...and our two heroes.

events.summary: The Altares y Muertos Tour is free and open to all, and it has become one of the most popular and beloved activities of the Milagro Central Eastside Muertos Celebration. Beginning at 11:30 AM, participants assemble in El Zócalo, the community gathering space at El Centro Milagro, and each guest is gifted a garland of silk marigolds to decorate themselves and their bicycles. Sometimes called zempachule or Flor de Muerto \(Flower of the Dead\), the marigold is an integral symbol of Día de Muertos. With their bright orange- and yellow-colored petals and strong fragrance, marigolds are believed to have the power to guide the souls of the dead back into the world of the living. At 12:00 PM, the first group of participants departs on a route around Portland’s Central Eastside, stopping intermittently at these partner businesses that are hosting altars as part of the Altares y Muertos Public Art Exhibition: Bar Botellón – 606 NE Davis St. Portland, OR 97214 Cargo – 81 SE Yamhill St. Portland, OR 97214 Cumbia Corazón – 222 SE 8th Ave, Portland, OR 97214 El Zócalo @ El Centro Milagro – 537 SE Stark St, Portland, OR 97214 New Deal Distillery – 900 SE Salmon St, Portland, OR 97214 Nossa Familia Coffee – 1633 SE 3rd Ave, Portland, OR 97214 Point West Credit Union – 1107 NE 9th Ave, Portland, OR 97232 River City Bicycles – 534 SE Belmont St., Portland, OR 97214 Along the way, they are guided by volunteers from The Street Trust, helping ensure everyone’s safety. This year, altars will be on public display beginning Saturday, October 24 and may be viewed during each business’ normal operating hours through Friday, November 6. \(A link to the map of all tour locations will be available for download on this page beginning Friday, October 23.\) The Altares y Muertos Tour will include a brief stop at the second annual Blumenauer Bridge Witching Hour, which takes place that day, but no altar is on display at that event.
events.title: Altares y Muertos Tour

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: Fat Over Lean is a free art exhibition celebrating fat bodies, fat artists, and the many ways fatness intersects with queerness, disability, identity, and belonging. Curated by Portland artist Michelle Jackson, the exhibition brings together artwork by over 30 fat artists from across the Pacific Northwest, including painting, photography, fiber, ceramics, mixed media, and more. Created in response to the lack of positive and nuanced representation of fat bodies in the arts, Fat Over Lean is about making space for people whose bodies and experiences are too often left out of galleries. The exhibition will also feature free community events and creative programming throughout October. See works by Alexis Barnes, Ana Mai Luckett, Aurora Owen, Cherie Savoie Tintary, Eko Salamanca, Fi Bu, Garrett Stache, Heather Lobitz, Heather Weitman, Jessie Wu, Jo MahnkeVanHuss, Johnny Sheckler, JUUPI, KT Kusmaul / Body Home Fat Dance, Laura Grae Miller, Lyzz Stewart, M. V. Moran, Madison Flickinger, McKinley Johnson, Michelle Jackson, Morgan Wilhelm, Nat & Jess Breece, Richelle Fullerton, Roselynn La Jeunesse, Ruby Webb, Shaun Crabb, Shayla Smith, Shelby Fercik, Miss Joomina, Sossity Chiricuzio, Stevie Rosman-Hyde, Tarina Bagua, and Uwin Hakan. Join us for these upcoming events: Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3rd, 3- 8 p.m. Why Don't I Draw Myself Fat? Saturday, October 24th from 6 - 7:30 pm. A miniature Art Show and Telltale night of storytelling and taking up space in community hosted by Telltale Presents Closing Reception/Halloween Party: Saturday, October 31st, 7 - 9 pm. About Fat Over Lean Fat Over Lean is a project that aims to lower barriers to the arts for fat, queer, and disabled people by creating opportunities to share their work within the greater Portland, Oregon, and southern Washington communities. Artists were not charged a fee to apply for this show, and they will not pay a commission on artwork sold during the exhibition, aside from standard transaction fees. We believe artists should be able to share their work without having to navigate unnecessary financial barriers. By supporting fat artists, creators, and educators, Fat Over Lean hopes to create more opportunities for growth, visibility, advancement, and connection. This project is about making room: for fat bodies, for queer and disabled voices, for artists who are often asked to take up less space, and for the communities that grow when we get to show up as ourselves. This project was made possible by RACC, Portland Arts & Culture, Fans Only Studio, and Portland Clean Air Committee. Visit Fat Over Lean or Michelle's Instagram for events and gallery hours.
events.title: Fat Over Lean Art Show & Free Events

Featuring a series of vignettes following the connective thread - “what makes a man a monster,” this fever dream production is a 55 minute runaway train of hilarious and haunting witches, bloody battles, and macabre madness - the perfect way to spend your Halloween weekend! Our audience is invited to meet at the oversized sidewalk chess set at the southeast corner of Director Park, and follow the Three Weird Sisters to a nearby outdoor arena. Trick or Treat bags are available before the show, because even adults deserve a little treat on Halloween. Walk-up audiences are welcome throughout the show, and this production is entirely FREE - though donations and tips to our hard working cast and crew are encouraged. Speculative Drama is a program under Misfit Academy, a performance oriented 501(c)3 and all donations and tips are 100% tax-deductible. Please note: All actors are fully vaccinated and tested day-of, audience masks are heavily encouraged for the safety of the actors. Anyone wearing a mask will be treated to a special gift, thank you for helping us keep our community safe and healthy! THE EXPERIENCE Our annual Halloween Hausu screening returns! Buckle up for House \(Hausu\)-a genre-defying fever dream that feels as fresh, bizarre, and hilarious today as it did in 1977. Part haunted house horror, part surreal comedy, part pop-art collage, Nobuhiko Ôbayashi's cult classic is the cinematic equivalent of opening a haunted toy box: playful, chaotic, and bursting with color and invention. Whether it's your first visit to the aunt's mansion or a yearly pilgrimage, come ready to laugh, gasp, and surrender to the strange. ON SCREEN: House \(Hausu\) 1977. Directed by Nobuhiko Ôbayashi. Runtime: 88 minutes. In an effort to avoid spending time with her father and his creepy new lover, young Gorgeous \(Kimiko Ikegami\) resolves to visit her aunt's remote mansion. With six of her closest friends in tow, including the musically inclined Melody \(Eriko Tanaka\) and the geeky Prof \(Ai Matsubara\), Gorgeous arrives at the estate, where supernatural events occur almost immediately. A severed head takes flight, household appliances come to life and a portrait of a cat seems to contain an evil spirit. WITCHING HOUR

events.summary: The year is 2056. We always knew they were out there…we just didn’t know they would attack so soon. Our city has fallen. Alien invaders and their cyborg forces have reduced the streets to rubble, and the few remaining survivors are doing whatever they can to escape. As if that weren’t enough, the destruction has brought another threat out of the shadows: zombies. This year’s interactive, no-contact haunted theatre drops you into the middle of the invasion. Choose how you face the apocalypse: Join the Resistance Rent an optional laser-tag weapon \(\+$2\) and fight back. The equipment uses a safe, invisible infrared beam to activate designated targets and trigger special effects as you move through the theatre. Become a Refugee Prefer not to use laser tag? Make your way through the ruined city as a refugee, trying to escape with your life while danger waits around every corner. Apocalypse in the Grove may include fog, laser lighting, loud noises, strobe effects, simulated fire, cold sparks, sudden scares, and intense theatrical environments. Will you join the resistance—or simply try to survive? When you purchase a ticket, you purchase a reservation for a 30 minute window. You must arrive in this timeframe or your entry could be delayed or denied. There are 6 people in each tour of the haunted theatre. This experience is wheelchair accessible. Children 12 and under MUST be accompanied by an adult.

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. Show Dates: October 15 – November 1, 2026 Thu – Sat at 7:30pm, Sun at 2pm Special Dates: Thursday, October 15 is a preview performance, with discounted tickets. Friday, October 16, is Opening Night! Sat, Oct. 24th – ASL Interpreted Performance Sun, Oct. 25th – Audio Described Performance
events.title: The Woman In Black

events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill
