events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm

Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: Lost Staged Readings October 2nd & November 6th from 5 pm - 7 pm Theatrical readings inspired by the theme "Lost". Stop by on First Friday in October or November to catch performances running from 5 PM - 7 PM. MPA will be open to the public, donations are appreciated but not required. Words, Words, Words recalls the philosophical adage that three monkeys typing into infinity will sooner or later produce Hamlet and asks: What would monkeys talk about at their typewriters? Sure Thing: Two people meet in a café and twist their way through a conversational minefield as an offstage bell interrupts their false starts, gaffes and faux pas on the way to falling in love. The Items Forgotten: A married couple, Kira and Travis, get locked out of their house on a very cold winter evening for the third time in a single week. As they hunt for a spare key on the porch, they begin to question both their state of mind and their relationship. Alfred and Lily and Their Marvelous Tank in the Forest: Alfred and Lily are evacuated from their local pond—supposedly for renovations—and placed inside a mysterious tank by unseen "benefactors". While Lily loves the new environment and trusts their handlers, Alfred notices horrifying signs: the water is drying up, neighboring creatures are disappearing, and things are not as idyllic as they seem. WRITTEN BY David Ives and Tara Meddaugh DIRECTED BY Dylan Sladky RATED PG-13 RUN TIME 30 minutes

events.summary: The Haven PDX Presents: First Friday Art Walk Join us at our new location at 2505 NE Pacific Street for Portlands first Friday art walk. A visionary ecosystem where artists, healers, and cultural innovators unite talents to cultivate a transformative collective experience. ​For the past five years, The Haven has hosted immersive art experiences, pop-up events, workshops, and large-scale community activations across the city, weaving together a vibrant network of creatives and entrepreneurs. ​Now entering a new era, The Haven has been reborn as a regenerative sanctuary for creativity, wellness, and collective enterprise. What was once a site of industrial production is being transformed into a living cultural hub. Where imagination, healing, and collaboration give rise to new models of shared prosperity! ​The Haven is stewarded by a cooperative of artists, builders, wellness practitioners, and mission-driven businesses who share a commitment to community, and cultural regeneration. Together, we’re cultivating a space that functions as both an art gallery and a dynamic ecosystem. Hosting studios, galleries, wellness practices, and creative enterprises that are synergizing to inspire and support one another. ​We aren't just a simple art gallery, we are building an economy of imagination, wellness, and collective growth.!

events.summary: A D&D game, a Shakespeare company, and a nonprofit walk into a strip club… Portland’s immersive storytellers and alternative arts nonprofit Misfit Academy 501(c)(3) is about to turn 14 and we’re throwing A Joyful Trouble, a very special party with all our favorite people, full of what we’re known for - immersive world building, story based performance, a little bit of Shakespeare, and a healthy dose of sultry! Celebrate Portland’s only multidisciplinary and site-specific arts nonprofit, home of Speculative Drama, The Night Carnival, and Myrrh Larsen’s Song Sagas with some true “Portland weird” at this cocktail party and casual gala featuring a Dungeons & Dragons actual play game, raffle prizes, silent auction, dancers, cocktails, and more! For over a decade, Misfit Academy has brought world-class performing arts to unique spaces around Portland, growing from a tiny underground club into a thriving network of artists creating more than six theatre, cabaret, music, and circus productions a year. This November, we’re preparing for our fifteenth season of events with a fundraiser to support our permanent rehearsal and development space in the heart of downtown Portland! Whether you come to watch as our D&D players navigate the plot of a mystery Shakespeare play, bid on fantastic raffle prizes and silent auction items from some of Portland’s best artists and local businesses, or to mingle and enjoy the artistic atmosphere, “A Joyful Trouble” is just that - a celebration of all things beautiful, brilliant, and a little bit transgressive. Want to get in on the story? Become a Deus Ex Machina of the game with story-altering gameplay goodies for purchase, unlock celebrity cameos as we hit fundraising goals, or splurge on one of a very few VIP Player tickets and join the table yourself! Follow along at instagram.com/thenightcarnivalpdx as we announce celebrity cameo donations, special guest players, raffle and silent auction items, give some peeks behind the scenes…and make A Joyful Trouble! A note on accessibility: All venues are ADA accessible and accessible by public transit. Masks are highly encouraged for audience members. Performers will move throughout the venues, and audience members should be prepared to be within 6 foot proximity of unmasked performers and other audience members. Promotional designs by Myrrh Larsen
events.title: A Joyful Trouble - a fundraiser for Misfit Academy

The graveyard "maitre d," quickly realizes that there has been a misunderstanding in the hiring process and that he's been mistakenly hired for the precarious “night shift” position, one unfit for pedigree. He is about to experience nothing short of a fortuitous paranormal entanglement unlike any other. events.summary: TAIPEI CITY, TAIWAN Birdy Choreographer Lai Hung-chung makes dances of striking beauty and intention. Birdy, his captivating signature work for Hung Dance, moves between suspense and explosive energy, between the weight of tradition and the pull toward something new. Hung Dance seamlessly blends traditional Chinese arts – including Tai Chi, Peking Opera, and classical Chinese music – with current dance techniques and driving electronic music to create work that is poetic and flowing, rhythmic and impressive. What you see on stage is a work in constant transformation: bodies that bend and resist, images that linger, a world where the tension between holding on and letting go becomes the dance itself. Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. events.summary: Music of Resistance: A Tribute to Mikis Theodorakis On November 6, HACCM presents the Kombos Collective, with artists from San Francisco, the East Coast, and Portland for a performance devoted to the music of the late Mikis Theodorakis. Many will know Theodorakis for his film scores \(like the iconic "Zorba the Greek"\), but he was also a symbol of resistance throughout his life. Whether your taste runs to folk or classical music, this concert has something for you. The ensemble performs a range of Theodorakis' most treasured songs — pieces as historically significant as they are musically beautiful. This includes "Ballad of Mauthausen," set to the poetry of Holocaust survivor Iakovos Kambanellis, and widely regarded as one of the most beautiful songs ever written about the Holocaust. In addition to live music, attendees will learn about the enduring cultural significance of Theodorakis' music. This concert will be held at the PSU Lincoln Recital Hall at 1620 SW Park Ave. Concert begins at 7:30p.m. with a reception beforehand.
events.title: Music of Resistance: A Tribute to Mikis Theodorakis

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.
events.title: Anthropology

events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Classic cinema and innovative live music come together in this one-of-a-kind performance by acclaimed cellist and composer Gideon Freudmann. Performing an original live soundtrack to Sherlock Jr. using cello, looping, and real-time digital effects, he’ll transform this silent film masterpiece into a thrilling modern performance experience! In Sherlock Jr., Buster Keaton stars as a movie projectionist who dreams of becoming a great detective. Packed with inventive visual storytelling, legendary stunts, and timeless comedy, this 1924 silent classic remains one of Keaton’s most beloved and enduring films. The evening will begin with a live set showcasing Freudmann’s innovative original music, followed by a complete screening of the film with live musical accompaniment. Blending film, humor, and musical innovation, this unique event offers audiences a rare opportunity to experience a silent-film masterpiece reimagined through the artistry of a truly original musician.
events.title: Gideon Freudmann presents "Sherlock Jr."

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: 7pm doors, 8pm show All ages welcome Gully Boys The Gully Boys origin story begins in the aisles of a Minneapolis thrift shop. Vocalist/guitarist Kathy Callahan \(she/her\) and co-worker Nadirah McGill \(they/them\) spent their days sharing dreams and building a friendship amongst racks of forgotten treasures. When Kathy confided her desire to sing in a band, it set off a groundswell of events: Nadi grabbed a pair of drumsticks, and the two invited middle school friend Natalie Klemond \(she/her\) to join on bass. From there, a cover of Best Coast's "Girlfriend" marked the start of a journey fueled by undeniable chemistry, channeling the raw energy of legends like No Doubt, Garbage, and Hole into a sound that's galvanizingly Gully. Two years of relentless gigging followed, and earned Gully Boys the Best New Band crown by their local Minneapolis City Pages in 2018, shortly after the release of their debut demo collection, Not So Brave. Their anticipated follow-up EP, Phony, arrived in late 2019, just months before the live music world came to a halt. Inspired by this break in the action, the band added lead guitarist Mariah Mercedes \(they/them\), and worked with producer Zach Zurn at Carpet Booth Studio to release their Favorite Son EP \(2021\) and standout singles "See You See" \(2022\) and "Optimist" \(2023\). Grounded in a bond as fierce as their sound, Gully Boys' electrifying live performances have earned them spots on SXSW stages, Audiotree sessions, and tours alongside Nova Twins, Motion City Soundtrack, Destroy Boys, Bad Bad Hats, and more. From the iconic stage at Minneapolis' First Avenue to national gigs that defy expectations, Gully Boys capture an ethos of equal parts anger and tenderness-fueling a journey that feels like it's just getting started. Pollyanna Pollyanna are a three-piece New Jersey band - Jill Beckett \(vocals/guitar\), Daniel McCool \(drums\), and Brandon Bolton \(bass\) - blending elements of loud rock, pop and punk into an emotional roller coaster of fury and catharsis. Born from the DIY touring scene, Pollyanna have become a force in the tri-state music scene, fusing pissed-off, "burn the world down" energy with moments of queer joy, trans pride, and raw vulnerability. Following their I Surrender Records debut "Slime", the band are keeping momentum high with their razor-sharp new single "Gravedigger," recorded with Brett Romnes \(Hot Mulligan, Mom Jeans, The Front Bottoms\). With their new sophomore album, "Weirdo", Pollyanna are taking bold new steps, articulating the journey of trading hatred for joy, and they're just getting started.
events.title: Gully Boys @ Mission Theater w/ Pollyanna and special guests to be announced

How do I register? Register by filling out this quick form . Groups, families, and individuals welcome! Under age 18? We request that youth 15 and under volunteer with a parent/guardian. Youth 16 and older can volunteer on their own and will need to hand us a youth waiver form signed by their parent/guardian. Questions? Please check out our Volunteer FAQ webpage . Our team is also happy to assist! Reach us at volunteer@friendsoftrees.org volunteer@friendsoftrees.org or 503-595-0213. We look forward to planting together soon! events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: Run Time: 86 min. TICKETS $15 Doors 3:30 p.m.; Film 4 p.m. Select Showtime to Purchase Tickets Click here to learn more about accessibility at the Tomorrow Theater. THE EXPERIENCE We're excited to team up with MUBI for this screening of Eleanor Coppola's Making Marie Antoinette, a lush, intimate documentary about Sofia Coppola creating Marie Antoinette. The mother-daughter duo began creating this documentary at the beginning of the COVID lockdown, and Sofia finished the film after her mother passed in 2024. All attendees get access to 60 days of MUBI at mubi.com/pamcut . ON SCREEN: Making Marie Antoinette 2026. Directed by Eleanor Coppola. Runtime: 86 minutes. In 2005, Sofia Coppola shot her third feature film, Marie Antoinette, starring Kirsten Dunst and Jason Schwartzman, at the Palace of Versailles, securing unprecedented filming permission that had never before been granted to any production. Her mother, acclaimed documentarian Eleanor Coppola, accompanied her on set, capturing approximately eighty hours of footage chronicling her daughter's journey throughout the making of the film. This year, on the occasion of the 20th anniversary of the release of Marie Antoinette and in fulfilment of her mother's wish, Sofia Coppola reviewed that previously unseen material. Making Marie Antoinette explores the craftsmanship and care that brought the film to life, follows legendary costume designer Milena Canonero at work, and offers a glimpse into what it meant to be a young female director at that time. The result is a fascinating look at the creative process behind a landmark film and, at the same time, a surprisingly intimate family portrait. In the documentary, Eleanor Coppola's voice is performed by Academy Award® nominee Diane Lane, who reads excerpts from Eleanor's diaries, in which the filmmaker recounts her experience on set and reflects on her relationship with her daughter. ABOUT MUBI MUBI is a curated streaming service dedicated to elevating great cinema. Discover new ambitious works from iconic directors to emerging auteurs, all hand-picked by MUBI's team of curators. UNORTHODO
events.title: Making Marie Antoinette x MUBI

events.summary: The Portland Grief House invites you to join The Lost Table, a welcoming space to gather in community, remember those we’ve lost, and share in the traditions that help us keep them close. Bring a dish, pull up a chair, and make a place at the table for the dead. Grief can be hard to understand, and sometimes what we need most is community, ritual, conversation, and food. Together, we’ll explore how different cultures and traditions call to, honor, and make offerings to those who have died. In the spirit of Día de Muertos, we’ll create a shared space where the living and the dead can gather around the same table. We’ll begin with a creative activity led by Mario Mesquita, inviting us to reflect on memory, food, and our relationships with those we’ve lost. Participants will be introduced to the ritual elements that will carry us through the evening. Laura Green will lead a community conversation about intercultural traditions of Día de Muertos and other ways communities call to and remember their dead. Participants will have an opportunity to share stories, traditions, and memories, and to dedicate an offering to someone they have lost. Bea Yeh will introduce the tradition of Hungry Ghost and lead us in making an offering to the dead. We’ll set places at our table for those who are no longer with us and share food as an act of remembrance and connection. Our community offerings and tributes will be gathered at Ximena Morales’s altar, creating a shared space of remembrance that connects the different traditions and offerings brought into the room. Throughout the evening, we’ll create something together through words, offerings, and remembrance. We’ll dedicate a community poem to the dead and close our gathering with a collective ritual of words, sound, and stillness. Please bring: A dish to share, plus any serving utensils it needs. Consider bringing something that reminds you of a loved one or connects you to a family or cultural tradition. Please label your food with a card identifying any allergens or dietary considerations. Your own dinnerware \(plate, bowl, utensils, napkin\). A beverage for yourself, if you’d like something other than water. A photograph, name, or other small tribute to a loved one for the community altar, if you’d like. Please do not bring chips, salsa, or guacamole—Milagro will provide these. The Portland Grief House is honored to continue this tradition, originally started by Side Yard Farm. El Centro Milagro is excited to partner with Portland Grief House to create a space for English- and Spanish-speaking community members to gather, remember, share traditions, and honor the dead together. Schedule 4:00–4:30 PM — Opening Ritual & Activity 4:30–5:45 PM — Community Conversation & Offerings 5:45 PM — Dedication & Closing Estimated Running Time: 3 hours Age Recommendation: Ages 10\+
events.title: The Lost Table

events.summary: Harmonic Movement Contemporary Dance is a practice that invites each dancer to discover and infuse their own movement story and embodied voice into every movement and phrase. Drawing on the vocabularies of ballet, jazz, and modern dance, each class offers dancers of any age or experience level a way in that fits their own body, movement history, and expressive tendencies. A thorough warm-up helps dancers access their optimal strength and mobility, building both freedom and control before moving into playful and creative technique-building exercises and center choreography. At its heart, Harmonic Movement Contemporary Dance is about joy: the joy of movement, of dancing together, and discovering the ways creative expression can be genuinely healing.

events.summary: oin Baby Blues Connection for Mingle in the Moonlight, our annual celebratory evening of food, connection, conversation. Come for the delicious food and drinks. Mingle with fellow supporters and people who care about families. Enjoy a little friendly competition: browse the silent auction, try your luck with a mystery bag or wine wall, and stop by the photo booth to capture the moment. And in the middle of it all, we'll take 15 minutes to think about what it really means to become a parent. A Conversation About Matrescence This year's presentation features Dr. Kristen Seghete, who will introduce us to matrescence, the profound identity transition that happens as someone becomes a mother. In this brief presentation, Dr. Seghete will explore what matrescence is, why understanding it matters, and how changes in behavior connect with changes in the perinatal brain. She'll also touch on some of the long-term positive changes that can come with these brain and identity shifts. An Evening to Mingle The name says it all. We've intentionally built Mingle in the Moonlight around time to connect with other people. Doors open at 6:00 PM, with food, drinks, the silent auction and other activities opening shortly after. You'll have plenty of time to catch up with friends, meet new people and enjoy the evening before our brief presentation and fundraising activities begin. Evening highlights include: Catered food from Frontera Sur Drinks and plenty of time to mingle Silent auction Mystery bags with surprises valued at $25, $50 and more Wine wall featuring bottles valued at $25+ Photo booth A short presentation from Dr. Kristen Seghete Live auction and paddle raise The silent auction closes at 8:15 PM, followed by the presentation, live auction and paddle raise. The event officially ends at 9:00 PM, but you're welcome and encouraged to keep the conversation going a little longer. Your ticket includes a catered spread from Frontera Sur, featuring a variety of Latin American-inspired bites, including: Beef and vegetarian empanadas Shrimp cocktail with tortilla chips Chicken and potato taquitos Vegetarian, vegan and meat chuchitos Small tostadas guatemaltecas Achiote chicken, vegetable and steak skewers A selection of sauces Your Ticket Helps Families Mingle in the Moonlight is a fundraiser for Baby Blues Connection. We raise funds to help families find connection, information, resources and peer support when they're experiencing perinatal mood and anxiety disorders. The need for that support doesn't exist in a vacuum. Families are navigating rising costs for groceries, gas, utilities, housing and just about everything else. Even parents who have mental health insurance may face co-pays and other out-of-pocket costs that make getting help difficult. For some families, seeking mental health support can mean making a choice between getting the help they need and paying for the basics. We don't want parents to have to make that choice. And we're concerned about what happens when parents don't get support. A parent's mental health affects the whole family, including their children. Proceeds from Mingle in the Moonlight will help Baby Blues Connection keep our core programs available to families, support our volunteers and community connections, provide education and resource navigation, and cover the general operating costs that make this work possible. We're also working toward expanding hyper-local support so families can find connection closer to home and in the communities where they live.

The music is colored with world influences ranging from Indian classical, jazz, and psychedelic rock, enhancing the mood so each repetition of the Name can awaken the heart. Led by Sitaram Dass with Jeanette Kangas on tabla, Clark Stacer on bass, Lance Jordan on guitar, and a rotating selection of some of the PNWs finest musicians. Sitaram Dass (he/him) spent several years serving his beloved teacher Ram Dass on Maui, where he was shown the path of Bhakti, the yoga of service and devotion to God. He is an author, teacher, kirtan singer, and spiritual counselor. As the director of the Sacred Community Project, he works to provide affordable, free, and donation-based offerings as a praxis of Sacred Community. Net proceeds support the Sacred Community Project, an interspiritual service and art collective that works to “lower the barriers of access to contemplative and devotional practices.” $25 Advance / $30 Door (No one turned away for lack of funds)

events.summary: Portland based musician \(as well as a Newberg native\) Jackson Warner takes the stage with full band and horn section! Portland, Oregon–based musician Jackson Warner is carving his own lane in modern rock with grit, heart, and unwavering dedication. Rooted in the musical spirit of the Pacific Northwest, his sound blends classic rock swagger with raw, lived-in storytelling—capturing both the romance and reality of chasing a dream. His latest single, “Built for the Road,” is a fist-in-the-air rock anthem that pulls back the curtain on life as a working musician. Driven by punchy guitars, a relentless backbeat, and shimmering horns, the track explores long miles between gigs, uncertain paydays, and the emotional toll of pursuing a life in music. It’s a battle cry for artists, dreamers, and anyone who’s sacrificed comfort for calling. Known for electrifying live shows and no-frills authenticity, Warner channels the spirit of road-worn rock troubadours while staying grounded in the present. Whether playing to a packed venue or a dimly lit barroom, he brings the same intensity—turning every stage into a proving ground.

Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: Lila Forde and Zan FiskumSoul'd Out Presents: Lila Forde and Zan Fiskum. Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages 21+. Special Note: Ticket holders for this show receive free admission to Jack London's Burly Q Revue Cabaret after the music! LILA FORDE With a voice steeped in jazz, soul, folk, and old-school American songcraft, the Seattle-born, Los Angeles-based singer/songwriter has always carried a deep sense of self through her music. But on Life Can Still Be Sweet, her sophomore album, that self comes into fuller focus: A little older, a little wiser, more instinctive, and more firmly in command of the world she's building. Warm, whimsical, and full of growing pains, the record captures Forde in the thick of her twenties -- chasing songs, learning lessons, finding her people, and holding onto beauty even when life gets hard. , "rdquo" -> I think I have a really unique voice -- not just my literal voice, but my proverbial voice," Forde says. , "rdquo" -> In this day and age, and in this industry, there's a lot of trend following, and there's a lot of homogeny. I'm just really trying to be my own artist." That individuality has been there from the beginning. Raised in a spiritual, music-filled household in Seattle, Forde grew up without a television and with her feet in the dirt -- the daughter of a musician and meditation teachers who encouraged her to stay curious, grounded, and creatively free. She sang in choirs, studied jazz in college, and steeped herself in the classics, from Bonnie Raitt and Carole King to Ella Fitzgerald and Nancy Wilson, while developing her soulful California sound that feels unmistakably her own. https://lilaforde.com/ --- Zan Fiskum Zan Fiskum is a singer and songwriter from Maple Valley, WA, whose music blends folk, soul, and cinematic pop into emotionally vivid storytelling. Known for her commanding vocal range and a diversean diverse sound rooted in the Pacific Northwest, Zan has built a dedicated following through a series of independent releases that have amassed over a million streams. She has opened for artists including The Avett Brothers, Kingfish, Mon Rovia, and shared the stage with John Legend and Dave Matthews. https://zanmusic.net/ ---------- JLR Seating Map Notes: For this show, you may reserve individual tables on the map pictured. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm

That shy kid who taught himself guitar has spent nearly four decades bringing Denver's timeless songs to stages across the country, becoming the most celebrated interpreter of the beloved icon's catalog. A ROCKY MOUNTAIN HIGH EXPERIENCE® offers more than nostalgia—it's an authentic celebration of the music that defined a generation. Rick's heartfelt performances transport audiences through Denver's greatest hits: the sun-soaked warmth of "Sunshine on My Shoulders," the foot-stomping joy of "Thank God I'm a Country Boy," the soaring beauty of "Rocky Mountain High," and beloved classics like "Take Me Home, Country Roads," "Annie's Song," "Calypso," and "Leaving on a Jet Plane." Join us for an unforgettable evening celebrating the life, legacy, and enduring spirit of John Denver.

events.summary: When the nation and culture you grew up in and love have been taken over by a war-waging fascist dictatorship, how do you come to understand the nature and causes of what has happened? Perhaps you can do this only after you fled for your life. How then would you look at the ruins left inside yourself? This was the situation faced by one of the most sophisticated and profound thinkers of the twentieth century, Theodor Adorno \(1903–1969\), when he found himself living in Los Angeles during World War II after escaping from Nazi Germany. In this Delve we will study Adorno’s Minima Moralia: Reflections from Damaged Life—the amazing book he wrote between 1944 and 1949 to explore his feelings about the calamitous situation of a world facing despotism. We will read the entire book and focus on selected essays. The book is made up of 153 very short essays, ranging from 1-3 pages. The essays focus his philosophical genius on deeply observed and subtle aspects of ourselves that contribute to or resist the ways in which we are socialized that result in alienation, loss of will and agency, and unfulfillment. He explores consumer culture, the arts, and politics along with his recollections of the rise of fascism. Each essay is a deep and intricate knot of feelings and ideas, presented by a contemplative, perseverant, unblinking thinker of the highest order Although written in grief, Adorno always seeks hope by confronting, with maximum honesty and penetration, the deep roots of the problems human society faces. Minima Moralia is a monument to the sensitive study of culture and our psyches amidst disaster trauma. Adorno’s brilliant and strong style make this book a pleasure to think with. In this Delve we will read the entire book and focus on selected entries. Text: Minima Moralia: Reflections from Damaged Life
events.title: Theodor Adorno: Minima Moralia

Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. THE EXPERIENCE James Spooner joins PAM CUT for a screening of his film Afro-Punk, followed by an author talk for his new book It Starts With Anger. Books will be available for sale on site. IT STARTS WITH ANGER is a coming-of-age graphic memoir exploring race, identity, and rebellion through James Spooner's teenage years in 1990s New York into his young adulthood in the early 2000s. Confronted with systemic racism, microaggressions, and Nazi extremism within punk spaces, Spooner traces how reactionary anger evolved into a creative force and a path to self-determination, along the way following the founding of the Afro-Punk movement, his eventual decision to leave the company, and an ongoing raw examination of the tensions between underground culture and mainstream success. While not a traditional graphic memoir, IT STARTS WITH ANGER combines black and white zine-inspired visual elements including photos, illustrations, and cartoon panels with traditional narrative in a unique package that recounts the story behind Afropunk. James Spooner has not talked publicly about his reasons for quitting Afropunk previously and the book is a damning indictment of its corporatization. But more importantly it also oﬀers a look at issues of Black identity, representation, and the lack thereof in a movement that had often prided itself on allyship, while being completely myopic to all the ways it fell short in that regard as a scene that was ironically both liberating and alienating for the Black people drawn to it. ON SCREEN: Afro-Punk 2003. Directed by James Spooner. Runtime: 1 hour 6 minutes. This film, which many may assume is a historical punk documentary, actually is an honest and needed treatment of race and identity. Punk and Hardcore music is simply the microcosm in which it is told. First time Director, James Spooner, in telling this story, has opened new dialogues on these crucial subject both intra and interracially. Many times funny, sometimes sobering, a wake up call to America. An examination of the duality of racial identity that DuBois called "double consciousness." What could have been "The Bad Brains Story" is a story about kids, alienated by two cultures and two communities. Many of these punk and hardcore kids have never questioned their role in the punk scene or the black community until their interviews, and it's obvious as they struggle on camera to reconcile a fragmented self. ON STAGE: James Spooner James Spooner is an award-winning graphic novelist, filmmaker, and tattoo artist. His debut graphic novel, The High Desert, was named a Best Book of 2022 by Publishers Weekly, The Washington Post, and the New York Public Library. The book went on to receive the American Library Association's Alex Award and the Cartoonist Studio Prize. Spooner is the co-editor of Black Punk Now, an anthology of Black punk writers and comic creators. The collection was named one of the top music books of 2023 by Pitchfork, among the top five music books by The Guardian, and received a starred review from Kirkus. His forthcoming hybrid prose-and-comics memoir, It Starts with Anger, will be published by Pantheon Books on August 4. Spooner directed the seminal documentary Afro-Punk, which premiered at national and international film festivals including the Toronto International Film Festival and the American Black Film Festival. He also co-founded the Afro Punk Festival, which has grown to attract worldwide audiences in the hundreds of thousands. A Kickstarter campaign to restore and preserve Afro-Punk is slated to launch in May. His work has been featured in outlets including NPR, The Los Angeles Times, Vice, The Village Voice, The New Yorker, MTV, NBC News, and Variety. He is a recipient of the ReNew Media Rockefeller Grant, has served as a guest curator for the Broad Museum in Los Angeles and the Punk Rock Museum in Las Vegas, and previously programmed for the Brooklyn Academy of Music. events.summary: For thirty years, David Bazan has been writing about what it means to believe in something—and what it means when those beliefs fray. When Pedro the Lion released It's Hard to Find a Friend in 1998, Bazan was already a keen observer of moral and existential conflict, capturing minor human disappointments with devastating attention. By the time Control came out, his writing had sharpened, slicing through suburban politeness and the American dream with pinpoint precision. For over a decade, he built Pedro the Lion into one of indie rock's most quietly radical projects, chronicling doubt, faith, guilt, and the messy pursuit of grace in a way that felt both deeply personal and universally resonant. Then, in 2006, he retired the Pedro the Lion moniker, as if setting down an old burden. Bazan kept writing, releasing the synth project Headphones and five solo albums that were blunt and revelatory in their own right, but the decision to retire the name felt definitive. Until, suddenly, it wasn't. In 2017, after being dormant for more than a decade, Pedro the Lion was back. The deeply autobiographical albums to follow, Phoenix, Havasu and Santa Cruz, marked a return to the places that shaped him literally and metaphorically, tracing the lines of the past to understand the shape of the present. Now, on the occasion of Pedro the Lion's 30th anniversary, Bazan is doing what he does best: stepping onto a stage and making these songs feel brand new again. The anniversary shows are less about commemoration than they are continuation, a chance to revisit the entire 30 year catalog in a way that is still active, still evolving. "The name felt like an imaginary friend for me," he says, "a way to have a relationship with myself." But if Pedro the Lion was once an imaginary friend, it is now something else. It is less like a ghost from the past and more like an old companion you fall back in step with, no matter how much time has passed. For all the sorrow and searching that has shaped it, the music has always had an essential warmth—a belief in people, in possibility, and in the redemptive power of bearing witness to your own life. Three decades in, Pedro the Lion remains a project about faith, even if that faith has taken on new shapes. It's the persistent hope that there is meaning in the telling: if you lay it all out, every doubt and devotion, every failure and flicker of hope, something honest will emerge. - Danielle Dietze
events.title: Pedro the Lion & Earlimart

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

events.summary: Feeding the Future A collaborative group show organized by Alberta Street Gallery members Sasha Wilk and Gabe Wolfe. Both curating artists are parents of young children and have brought together other creatives who are caregivers, educators, or allies of children to showcase work that uplifts and celebrates youth. As citizens invested in hope for a future built on love and care, we know that the next generation requires our attention to nourish them into becoming the compassionate, responsible, and thoughtful humans the next chapter of humanity needs. The works in this show feature images centering play, connection, and collaboration as enriching elements of young people's lives. The artists: Sasha Wilk, Gabe Wolfe, Kyra Watkins, Elizabeth Goss, Stefania Salles Bruins, Corinne Kenly Barber, Forest Salazar, Danny Stephens and Kristie Winther. October 29 through November 22, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

Wander through a wonderland of locally made treasures, from ceramics, candles, textiles, and glass art to beanies, body care, bolo ties, sunCATchers, card games, journals, apparel, kitchen must-haves, and all kinds of artful things for your home and everyone on your list. One lucky winner will take home a gift basket featuring an item from each of our Holiday Market Artists in Residence vendors, plus an Artifact gift card. Raffle tickets are $5 each, and 100% of raffle proceeds will benefit Project Lemonade, supporting foster youth across Oregon. Want to give a little more? events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. events.summary: In rating Small Things Like These 41st on its list of the 100 Best Books of the 21st Century, the New York Times said: “Not a word is wasted in Keegan’s small, burnished gem of a novel, a sort of Dickensian miniature….” This is an important novella in the vein of Dickens’s A Christmas Carol, but with an ending that packs a different punch. At its center is a man torn between family, community, church, and one young woman in a terrible predicament. He must make a choice, and Keegan’s exquisite, concise writing reveals that agonizing choice. It’s a perfect story to ponder and discuss: What would you choose in his situation? Keegan’s other work, “Foster,” is a long short story with a big impact. No word is wasted as Keegan tells the story of a young girl sent to live with another family when her own mother is fraught with problems of her own. Again, in the New York Times’s glowing review they say: “Keegan makes us complicit in what her characters want, setting us up for utter heartbreak when they don’t get it.” Foster’s is already considered canonical and is taught as a required text for Comparative Literature in the curriculum for Ireland’s secondary schools. Join us in this two-week exploration of these incredible short works by an Irish writer of spare prose and mmense talent. Access Program We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available. Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions. Liaison position Every in-person class and seminar at Literary Arts has one liaison position. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts. Apply here for the liaison position.

events.summary: Our Foundation series is designed for anyone new to the practice of improvisation and for those wishing to re-learn or deepen their practice of the art form's basics. We welcome people from all backgrounds, both creative and non-creative, so no acting or performing skills are ever required: just a desire to have fun, trust your instincts, and learn! Students should expect to learn: 👂🏼New ways of listening 🎁 The gifts of staying in the moment 📚 Telling spontaneous stories with others 👣 Thinking on our feet & trusting our instincts 👥 Quickly collaborating with others 👀 Identifying & using non-verbal communication 💪🏼 Discovering our strengths Why Take Classes With Us? Change Through Play's studio is founded on the belief that student progress only comes from providing clear instruction and feedback. We not only want our students to learn the core skills of improvisation, but we also want them to IMPROVE over their time with us. Because of that, we offer learning opportunities that students won't find anywhere else, including: A safe, nurturing, and supportive environment 10 students max per class, so each gets lots of attention Coaching and check-ins throughout each class Blackboard discussions, to help visual and analytical learners Closing every class with students recognizing their own wins Receiving highly personalized notes from your teacher, celebrating your wins during the class series & recommending skills to work on when you come back for another class with us. Participating - for those who wish! - in our student showcases Receiving and reviewing vids & pics from our showcase as keepsakes and learning tools

events.summary: On her third album with Oh Boy Records, and her fifth since beginning her career a decade ago, Emily Scott Robinson once again unveils her mastery as a performer and storyteller. With her 2026 release Appalachia — recorded at Dreamland Recording Studios with Grammy-nominated producer Josh Kaufman — Robinson opens herself up to experimentation and sings in her crystal-clear voice about resilience, love, grief and hope. Robinson’s talent is no surprise to the music industry — she’s now a veteran touring artist, both at home and abroad. Her records Traveling Mercies \(2019\) and American Siren \(2021\) each landed high on Rolling Stone’s “Best Country and Americana Albums” and Stereogum’s “10 Best Country Albums” year-end lists. “There’s this thing I do with every record I make,” she says. “I knit a prayer into it, and I ask for all these songs to find their way to everyone who needs them. I ask these songs to be of service, to help people find and experience joy.” The diner where the waitress knows everyone by name. The World War Two veteran reflecting on the end of his life. The windswept trailer park where people prefer to keep their curtains closed. As she meditates on human frailty and the power of resilience, Robinson is at times vulnerable, at others, defiant and absolutely free. Rolling Stone called “Traveling Mercies” a collection of “country-folk songs about America in all its pain and glory with the literate, Southern gothic sensibility of Flannery O’Connor.” Robinson is on the rise with her new record— a tour de force from an elegant chronicler of her own existence and those of her fellow humans.
events.title: Emily Scott Robinson

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Both curating artists are parents of young children and have brought together other creatives who are caregivers, educators, or allies of children to showcase work that uplifts and celebrates youth. As citizens invested in hope for a future built on love and care, we know that the next generation requires our attention to nourish them into becoming the compassionate, responsible, and thoughtful humans the next chapter of humanity needs. The works in this show feature images centering play, connection, and collaboration as enriching elements of young people's lives. The artists: Sasha Wilk, Gabe Wolfe, Kyra Watkins, Elizabeth Goss, Stefania Salles Bruins, Corinne Kenly Barber, Forest Salazar, Danny Stephens and Kristie Winther. October 29 through November 22, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

events.summary: Meet new friends, learn the joys of improvisation, and transform how you communicate & collaborate in a supportive community! This daytime course is designed for students with open schedules who crave a fun, open, and safe environment in which to play and develop new skills. During our class series, we'll teach participants traditional improv skills that emphasise FUN, TEAMWORK, and COMMUNICATION, not preparing for performance. Expect a ton of joyful silliness! Why Take Classes With Us? Our studio is founded on the belief that student progress comes both from personal discovery and from teachers/facilitators who provide clear instruction and feedback. We not only want our students to learn the core skills of improvisation, but we also want them to improve their skills over their time with us. Because of that, we offer learning opportunities that students won't find anywhere else. All of our students will receive the following: A safe, nurturing, and supportive environment 10 students max per class, so everyone gets lots of attention Flexible class options to suit your budget & schedule Coaching and check-ins during & after each game to help make sure you've understood the breakthroughs Blackboard discussions during class, when necessary, to help visual and analytical learners Closing each class by recognizing our own wins Participating - for those who wish! - in our student showcases

Wander through a wonderland of locally made treasures, from ceramics, candles, textiles, and glass art to beanies, body care, bolo ties, sunCATchers, card games, journals, apparel, kitchen must-haves, and all kinds of artful things for your home and everyone on your list. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual.
